content.comment_body: I'm experiencing issues transferring programs via a 2GB SD card provided complimentary by [company_name]. I'm working with [product_name] [version_no] PLC and [product_name] [version_no] software. Programs are written in ladder logic and saved with the .LLD extension. Transfers using an Ethernet cable between PC and PLC work fine, retaining the LLD format. However, when I attempt to transfer programs from the SD card to the PLC, I receive an 'UNKNOWN CARD' error. I am able to copy the program from the PLC to the SD card, but the resulting file is named LOGO_U_P.BIN, which cannot be opened in the software. I would appreciate guidance on using the memory SD card to transfer programs in LLD format between devices.

To access the LOGO_U_P.BIN file, insert the memory card into your PC. Use [product_name] [product_name] software, and from the 'File' menu, choose 'Open' and select the BIN-file from the memory card directory.

Thanks for your prompt assistance. Following your instructions, I managed to open the file transferred from PLC to PC as LOGO_U_P.BIN and convert it to LLD format (LOGO_U_P1.LLD). However, I'm still unable to transfer a program from the SD card into the PLC. I also tried to save a program made on the PC as a BIN file but couldn't do so. Can you advise how to save a file to the memory SD card and successfully transfer it into the PLC?
The memory card can only contain a file named LOGO_U_P.BIN for the PLC to recognize it. No other file names are permitted.

Thanks to everyone for their help. Limitations on file naming and formats with the memory card are making transfers between PC and PLC challenging. Now I can use the card, but only with the LOGO_U_P.BIN file name. This restriction is inconvenient for [product_name] [version_no]; earlier versions allowed varied file names and formats, such as LLD and FBD.

I’d like to share my experience: The process requires having a base (.BIN) file obtained by transferring the program from the [product_name] base module to the memory card, then copying that file to the PC. When editing, you need to manually choose the .BIN format while saving, then transfer this back to the memory card. Insert the card into the [product_name] base module to transfer the program. I found it isn't possible to save a new circuit directly in the .BIN format, so keeping the correct file name is essential.

To clarify: 1) The [product_name] base module will only load a program from a memory card if the file is named LOGO_U_P.BIN. 2) Any file can be stored if the SD card is connected to the PC. 3) To transfer a program so that the base module reads it: a) Plug the card into a PC and use LSC's 'save as BIN' feature, ensuring the card is selected (subfolders aren't supported). b) Transfer the program to [product_name], and in the transfer dialog, you can also send it to an SD card (works on [version_no] and [product_name] [version_no]). c) Copy the program on the base module directly onto the memory card. While you'll set a program name, only the correct file name allows the base module to read it. Hope this clarifies the process.

analysis.insight_summary: Users encountered significant usability issues when trying to transfer programs between PC, PLC, and memory SD card using [product_name] software and [product_name] modules. Restrictive file naming ('LOGO_U_P.BIN') and format requirements (LLD/LAD vs BIN) caused confusion, hampering efficient workflows. The inability to utilize flexible file names and formats for SD card transfers negatively impacted user experience, especially compared to previous versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect smooth program transfers between PC and PLC using an SD card, along with the option to use descriptive file names and formats (LLD). Backward compatibility and convenience on par with earlier [product_name] versions are also anticipated.
